title: A layer can change what is underneath it: blur, pixelate, greyscale, invert
goal: Right now a blur softens the shape you drew, not the picture under it, so there is no way to blur an email address, pixelate a name, grey out a region or invert part of a screenshot. Add a layer whose job is to change what is beneath it: you draw a box (or any shape), pick what it does - Blur, Pixelate, Greyscale, Invert, Brighten or Darken - and everything under that shape is drawn through it. Each one has its own setting: blur has a strength, pixelate has a block size, greyscale and brightness have an amount. It is a normal layer in every other way: it moves, resizes, rotates, rounds its corners, takes a border or a shadow, sits in the layer list, and undoes.
notes:
Asked for by the user on 2026-09-09, after rejecting a dedicated redaction tool: "We need a much more powerful and generalized way to mix layer content onto the page to enable things like burn text on a layer, inverse it, pixelate it, greyscale it, and there needs to be a way to control the effect. Pixelation might have a granularity level, blur might have strength... are these effects or a property of the layer?"

SUPERSEDES the decision card 'hide-a-name-or-an-email-in-a-screenshot-before-y...', which the user resolved 'd' (do not build) the same day. The redaction case falls out of this general mechanism for free. Do NOT resurrect a dedicated cover-up or redact tool; the user called that "stupid and proprietary for a niche scenario".

Where it goes, and why. The answer to "effect or property" is NEITHER: it is the layer's CONTENT. The rule the app already keeps is Content = what a layer IS (a picture, a shape, a magnifier), Appearance = what it HAS, Effects = what you ADDED on top of it. EffectKind (Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerEffects.swift:20) is explicitly about the layer's own pixels - its comment says a blur is 'the layer's own softness, laid over everything it is made of'. An adjustment does the opposite: its input is what is BELOW. Putting it in the Effects list would give one list two meanings, so add a case to LayerContent (Sources/PhotonzCore/Layer.swift:886) beside .zoomCallout instead. A lens layer can then still wear its own Effects - a border round a blurred box, a shadow under it - which is exactly what a redaction callout wants.

The seam already exists and is already tested by the zoom callout. DocumentRenderer.swift:442 builds `backdrop` (output composited over underlay) for a zoom callout, and DocumentRenderer.swift:736 crops and transforms it. A zoom callout IS this feature with 'magnify' as its adjustment. Build the new kind next to it on the same path with a CoreImage filter on the end: CIGaussianBlur, CIPixellate, CIColorControls (saturation 0) or CIPhotoEffectMono, CIColorInvert, CIColorControls (brightness). Then mask to the layer's shape and corner radii.

Traps a naive fix hits:
1. A lens must never read itself or anything above it, at any nesting depth, or it feeds back. Read only what is composited below.
2. The pass-through fast path at DocumentRenderer.swift:430 skips buffering a plain group and composites children straight onto the output. Check what that does to a lens inside such a group before assuming the underlay is right.
3. Blur and pixelate are NEIGHBOURHOOD operations: they read pixels from outside the layer's own frame, so cropping the backdrop to the frame first gives a dark or smeared edge. Sample wider than the frame, filter, then crop.
4. CIPixellate's blocks are anchored to a point, so a lens that is moved must not shimmer as its block grid slides; decide and record whether the grid is anchored to the canvas or to the layer.
5. Contentscale: the renderer draws at contentScale for zoom. A blur strength and a pixel block size are in document points and must scale with it, the same way ZoomCalloutOverlayRasterizer handles it (DocumentRenderer.swift:453 onwards), or a 10pt block is a different size at 200%.

Safety note worth one tooltip, not a second mechanism: what leaves the app (export, copy) is flattened, so a pixelated region really is gone from the PNG. The saved .photonz file still holds the original picture underneath. Say that once; do not build a separate baking step for it.

Explicitly OUT of scope, file as a follow-up: folding the existing zoom callout into this as a 'Magnify' adjustment. It is the right end state and the model should be shaped so it can happen, but the callout has canvas-space chrome (leader lines, source outline) and is shipped, so do not risk it in the same change.

See also the sibling task on blend modes - that is the OTHER axis (per-pixel maths against the backdrop, for tinting and burning) and it cannot do blur or pixelate, which are not blends. The two are complementary, not alternatives.
acceptance: A new layer kind exists that reads what is composited below it and draws it through a chosen adjustment; the shape of the layer is what it covers

The first set of adjustments all work and all have a setting you can change and see change live: Blur (strength), Pixelate (block size), Greyscale (amount), Invert, Brightness (amount, both directions)
The setting lives in the panel with everything else and reads as a setting of the layer, not as a second Effects list; a first-time user can find it without being told
The layer keeps everything a layer has: move, resize, rotate, corner radius, opacity, its own border and shadow, layer-list position, undo and redo
A lens over a group reads the group's contents over the canvas beneath the group, the same rule the zoom callout already follows, and a lens never reads itself at any nesting depth
Export and copy carry what you see: a pixelated region is pixelated in the PNG that leaves the app, checked by sampling exported pixels rather than by eye
Pixel tests in PhotonzRender for each adjustment, and model tests in PhotonzCore for the new content kind and its Codable round trip, all written before the implementation
A playtest walk covers drawing one, changing its adjustment, changing its setting, and moving it over different content
Audit under queue/audits/ with before and after captures of each adjustment, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) NOT a new Effects entry and not six tools: one LayerContent case (.lens) with an adjustment picked in the tool settings capsule before you draw and in the panel after, so the toolbar gains ONE slot, not six. (2) Cut from the mock idea: a separate shape enum. A lens is its box plus the corner radii every layer already has, so max radius gives the circle and the corner handles already round it. (3) Cut: baking/flatten step. Export already flattens. (4) Kept from the task notes: canvas-anchored pixelate grid, sample-wider-then-crop for blur and pixelate, settings in document points scaled by magnified(by:). (5) Found a gap the task did not name: a backdrop-reading layer rendered ALONE (layer thumbnail, drag sprite) has no backdrop, so a lens row in the layers panel would be blank and a drag would show nothing. Fix: a lens is never sprited (same refusal the zoom callout already has) and its thumbnail crops the real composite instead of rendering the layer alone. (6) Known limit, will land in rough: a ROTATED lens rotates the picture it samples, exactly as the zoom callout does today.

Built. PhotonzCore/Lens.swift holds LensAdjustment (blur, pixelate, greyscale, invert, brightness), LensContent (each adjustment keeps its OWN number, so switching and switching back hands your setting back), LensBuilder, Layer.lens/readsBackdrop/backdropSource, and a new .lens case on LayerContent. PhotonzRender/LensFilter.swift does the five filters; DocumentRenderer now builds the backdrop for ANY layer that answers readsBackdrop, so nothing can read itself at any depth. Lengths (blur sigma, block side) are scaled in Layer.magnified(by:), deliberately unclamped, so a 2x export blurs just as hard. The pixelate grid is anchored to the canvas origin, not the lens, so a nudged lens does not boil. RenderDiff now propagates over backdropSource rather than magnifiedSource, so a change under a lens redraws it. App: Tool.lens on K, one new tool-bar slot after the zoom callout behind next-lens, two settings in the capsule, a Lens section in the panel with a Does row and one slider (none for Invert), preview-then-commit so a slider pull is one undo step. A lens is never sprited during a drag and its layers-panel tile crops the real composite.

Adversarial review of the built thing, on the probe. Every adjustment reads right on a real screenshot, blur leaves no dark rim, the layer row renames itself and its tile shows the adjusted strip, Invert correctly shows no slider, moving the lens re-reads what it landed on, rounding rounds the region, undo steps back. Rough, all in the audit: a rotated lens turns the picture it samples (the zoom callout does the same); the live draft while dragging is a hairline box, not the adjustment; a Brightness lens at nought is invisible on the canvas. Two follow-ups filed: a-zoom-callout-becomes-a-magnify-lens and a-lens-turned-on-its-side-still-shows-the-pictur.

Lens layers shipped in Next behind next-lens: a new .lens LayerContent kind (PhotonzCore/Lens.swift) drawn by DocumentRenderer through LensFilter (blur, pixelate, greyscale, invert, brightness), a Lens tool on K in the tool bar, two settings in the capsule and a Lens section in the panel. Verified by 24 core tests, 18 pixel tests including an export sampled pixel by pixel, Scripts/test.sh green (5543 tests), and Scripts/playtest/lens-walk.json driven on the probe with real screen captures. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-12-lens.json. Two follow-ups filed; a full sweep requested because the bar gained a slot.
